candidates.title: How to repair faulty Industrial Rail couplers
candidates.excerpt: Many years ago, I purchased an O gauge Industrial Rail No. 5003 gondola. It’s a good-looking freight car, but it sometimes uncouples from the rest of its train, usually when rounding a curve but sometimes when it goes over a switch. Do you know if there is a way to repair it? — Stephen Greene Industrial Rail was started by United Model Distributors (UMD) in 1998 and produced a broad range of affordable, traditionally sized O-27 freight cars. The models were made well and featured excellent paint and graphics. Unfortunately, the company lasted only a few years. Production ceased around 2003 or 2004; Atlas purchased the line in 2006. Industrial Rail cars use a variant of Lionel’s magnetic disc coupler design, which first appeared in 1957. The knuckle is held in the closed position by an upward-facing pin on the end of a thin steel armature plate. The plate also has a downward-facing metal disc resembling a large thumbtack. candidates.title: Container freight rates rebound as Asia-Europe indexes diverge
candidates.excerpt: Global container freight rates showed signs of recovery in the latest weekly assessments, with all four major composite benchmarks recording increases. However, the improvement was far from uniform across individual trade lanes, particularly on Asia-Europe, where two leading indexes reported sharply different movements. Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) increased 3%, while the Freightos Baltic Index (FBX) rose 2%. China’s Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI), China Containerized Freight Index (CCFI) and Ningbo Containerized Freight Index (NCFI) also advanced. The latest figures suggest an improvement in overall freight rate conditions, although contrasting developments across the Transpacific, Asia-Europe and Transatlantic markets underline the uneven nature of the recovery. Chinese freight indexes move higher The SCFI increased 0.42% to 3,679.58 points in its 16 October assessment, compared with 3,664.11 in the previous reading. candidates.title: CMA CGM names methanol-powered Lorenzaccio
candidates.excerpt: CMA CGM has officially named CMA CGM Lorenzaccio, its latest 15,000 TEU methanol dual-fuel container ship. The vessel joins a series of six CMA CGM containerships named after characters from French literature. Lorenzaccio takes its name from the protagonist of the play by French writer Alfred de Musset. Under the command of Captain Predrag Vojvodic, CMA CGM Lorenzaccio will be deployed on the carrier’s Red Sea Express 2 (REX2) service. The weekly REX2 service connects major Asian ports with destinations in the Red Sea, including Djibouti, Jeddah, Ain Sokhna and Aqaba. The addition of CMA CGM Lorenzaccio expands the carrier’s methanol-capable fleet as CMA CGM continues investing in vessels designed to operate with alternative marine fuels.

According to Maersk, the project provided operational experience involving ethanol infrastructure, sourcing, supply-chain readiness and vessel operations. candidates.excerpt: The role of foreign companies in operating major container terminals remains a subject of debate, particularly when international investment intersects with national interests and the management of strategic infrastructure. Other approaches, including unrestricted foreign operations and operations subject to safeguards, also attracted support, while exclusively domestic operations represented a smaller share of the overall response. candidates.title: Tanker earnings defy all historical comparisons
candidates.excerpt: The tanker market has entered such extraordinary territory that independent owners could be making an additional $400m a day above their original earnings expectations, a windfall that, if sustained for a year, would almost match the entire container shipping industry’s profits during its pandemic-era boom. In its latest weekly report, broker Hartland estimates that independent owners of VLCCs, suezmaxes and aframaxes/LR2s are collectively generating around $400m in daily profits above what they budgeted at the start of 2026. The shipbroker calculates that a month of such earnings represents approximately $12bn in additional profits. A quarter would generate $36bn, while a full year would produce an astonishing $146bn. For context, the world’s containerlines made an estimated $150bn in 2022, their most profitable year on record. CSX operations chief to retire
candidates.excerpt: CSX Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Mike Cory is retiring, ending a tenure that began when he came out of retirement to join the railroad in September 2023. Cory will work with the leadership team to ensure a smooth transition, the company said, and will provide transition services through May 8, 2027. Rather than immediately naming a successor, CSX (NASDAQ: CSX) said two senior operations executives will now report directly to President and Chief Executive Steve Angel: - Doug Ryhorchuk, senior vice president of Operations, who oversees transportation, engineering, and mechanical functions. He spent nearly four decades at CN before joining CSX in 2024. - Casey Albright, senior vice president of Network Operations and Service Design, who has nearly 30 years at CSX.
